players.product: Advanced-packaging inspection/metrology (Dragonfly G5, 3DI) + JetStep panel-level lithography

quarterly_data.signal: H2 2026 margin outlook (CFO Brian Roberts): 'While cognizant of continued headwinds, for example, around certain material input costs, fuel surcharges, and freight expense', Onto anticipates additional gross margin expansion of an incremental 50 basis points per quarter in Q3 and in Q4; operating margin to rise 200 basis points to 32% in Q3 and to exit the year at an operating margin of 33% or higher. The Q3 EPS midpoint of ~$2.28 assumes a non-GAAP tax rate of 15% and slightly more than 50 million shares outstanding.
quarterly_data.figure: GM +50 bps per quarter in Q3 and Q4; operating margin 32% in Q3, 33% or higher exiting 2026; tax rate 15%

quarterly_data.signal: 2027 view (management, no formal plan yet). CEO Michael Plisinski on advanced packaging: 'We expect that to grow again into next year. We're not seeing any signs of overcapacity. We're hearing about constraints and pressure from our customers' customers on ramping more capacity'. CEO: 'we're not really prepared to talk about 2027 yet. However, we don't see any reason we can't continue to outperform the market', citing new-product SAM expansion, Dragonfly demand in advanced packaging, the metrology suite in advanced nodes and 'some incremental opportunities perhaps with the Rigaku partnership'; SoIC is one of the areas where the Dragonfly G5's higher resolution opens new opportunities, and based on customer feedback 'we're not expecting any kind of headwinds going into next year. We're expecting quite nice tailwinds.' The Dragonfly G5 mix 'is going to increase', not yet quantified. CFO Brian Roberts on 2027 gross margin: the extended-factory gains continue to scale, 'hopefully, with some ASP growth as the mix changes' as the G5 becomes a bigger share; the CEO expects continued gross- and operating-margin advances in 2027.

Demand and order pattern (CEO Michael Plisinski): orders do not arrive in steady streams — after a VPA is negotiated a large chunk of orders follows, mostly in the last month — so book-to-bill is hard to read; 'the general feeling is that backlogs are growing', and customers' growth plans and capex announcements are the better indicator. Demand through the semiconductor value chain 'remains high and gated by new fabrication facilities coming online', and customers provide Onto insights into their multi-year capacity plans. Growth is a mix of industry growth and share gains: 'If you look at our peers, I think we're growing above that', with new customers added and Dragonfly adopted in new areas 'at a much stronger pace than even we expected three months ago'. 'We're feeling pretty good about the back half of the year into the first part of 2027.'

Specialty and power: CFO Brian Roberts said other packaging and specialty device revenue, including power and SiC, declined sequentially in Q2 as expected but will rebound back to Q1 levels next quarter. CEO Michael Plisinski: if Power recovers, 'as we're starting to see some indications of', the Specialty market should start to grow next year, though 'That won't be close to the growth we're expecting from the packaging side.' Surface charge metrology is named among Onto's new market opportunities for 2027 and 2028.
